chapter: Radio color line, San Francisco and Columbia staff
title: Setting up the timpani; The Jolson Story and Rita Hayworth films
summary: Lee worked out how to arrange five timpani for crossovers and played traps on musicals including The Jolson Story.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Tell me about that first day. You got there an hour and a half early.

Oh, the first day was something. It came off, but it was -- you know, there's a trick to everything. In motion pictures, and in music, too -- you have to find out this particular thing, it was a matter of how to set the timpanies, you know, and by me being there that early, this is not tuning and you only tune them once, because you didn't have to change them; you didn't have time to change them because the thing -- I had the music someplace, and it went ba ba ba ba ba ba .. and that was it.

But it was where you had to end up and where you had to turn to start, because you're right in the middle of them. You've seen timpanies sitting right in the middle of them, and so we had 5, and he's back playing a role, and he's playing boom boom, you know, and then he's tuning this and tuning that -- but no, this carried themelodic line, you know, and that carried the whole thing to what she was doing and I stood there and figured out a way -- I kept moving them

around, moving them around, so the right hand would be -- wouldn't be in the way of the left when you crossed over, you know -- but I think from playing jazz, you know, that helped somewhat, because you play solos, and you cross over from tom tom to a thing like that, and so it's not difficult for you.

But it was an experience, and we also did the "Jolson Story" there, and did a couple of things on Rita Hayworth -- so actually, you see, what was happening was that I would be involved in the musicals, especially, because the guys couldn't keep time because they were legit. But my thing to do all the time was to play the traps, and to catch what they were doing.
